lines.text: In the days when the judges ruled, a famine hits, and Elimelech takes his wife Naomi and his sons Mahlon and Chilion to live in the land of Moab.
Elimelech dies, the sons marry Orpah and Rachel, and after the family had lived in Moab about ten years both sons die too, so Naomi is left without her husband and her two sons.

Naomi hears that the LORD has provided food for His people, so she sets out with her daughters-in-law on the road back to the land of Edom, and out on that road she tells them to go back to their mothers' homes.
Naomi's daughter-in-law tells her, "your people will be my people, and your God will be my God," and when Naomi sees that she is determined, she stops trying to persuade her.
Naomi and her daughter-in-law reach Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest, and Naomi tells the women to call her Mara because she went away full and the LORD has brought her back empty.
